_comment: CSRD scope as amended by the Omnibus package. These thresholds and dates are
the single most consequential thing this tool asserts, so they carry their
sources and a confidence grade like every factor in the register does.
Primary sources (EUR-Lex, EFRAG) could not be reached from the build
environment, so these are taken from professional-firm summaries and graded
medium rather than high. Verify against the directive before relying on them

sources.title: CSRD post-Omnibus revised scope and requirements

eu_company.note: Both conditions must be met. The Omnibus raised the employee threshold substantially and added a turnover test, taking a large number of previously in-scope companies out.

non_eu_group.note: Non-EU parent groups generating more than this in the EU.

waves.note: Companies already in scope continue reporting — FY2025 published in 2026, FY2026 published in 2027.
Deferred by the Omnibus from its original timetable.

simplified_esrs.note: The simplified ESRS set had not been published when this tool was built. It is expected to reduce the number of disclosures substantially and lean harder on materiality. Any datapoint-level gap analysis built against ESRS Set 1 (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772) is therefore provisional — which is why this tool works at standard level and says so rather than enumerating datapoints that are about to change.

standards.name: General requirements
standards.note: Sets the architecture rather than asking for disclosures — double materiality, reporting boundary, value chain, time horizons, and how to apply the topical standards. Nothing is filed against it directly, which is why its disclosure count is zero, but every judgement in this tool is made under it.

standards.name: General disclosures
standards.note: Applies in full regardless of the materiality assessment — the one standard a preparer cannot screen out. The twelve named disclosure requirements are listed. ESRS 2 also carries the minimum disclosure requirements for policies, actions, targets and metrics (MDR-P/A/T/M), which are not separate DRs but are applied through each topical standard, so they are not counted here.

drs.name: General basis for preparation of the sustainability statement
Disclosures in relation to specific circumstances
Role of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies
Information provided to and sustainability matters addressed by those bodies
Integration of sustainability-related performance in incentive schemes
Statement on due diligence
Risk management and internal controls over sustainability reporting
Strategy, business model and value chain
Interests and views of stakeholders
Material impacts, risks and opportunities and their interaction with strategy
Process to identify and assess material impacts, risks and opportunities
Disclosure requirements covered by the sustainability statement

standards.name: Climate change
standards.note: Assessed as material by almost every preparer, and the only topical standard where omission attracts an explicit explanation requirement. E1-6 is cross-linked to the GHG inventory in the evidence ledger — if an inventory exists, that DR already has evidence and its data quality score travels with it.

drs.name: Transition plan for climate change mitigation
Policies related to climate change mitigation and adaptation
Actions and resources in relation to climate change policies
Targets related to climate change mitigation and adaptation
Energy consumption and mix
Gross Scopes 1, 2, 3 and total GHG emissions
GHG removals and mitigation projects financed through carbon credits
Internal carbon pricing
Anticipated financial effects from physical and transition risks
